implementerProof.how: Six of its nine entries were re-run independently in the tester container against the same real PostgreSQL 17.11 + pgvector rig (the pod's containers share a network namespace, so the Postgres the implementer left on 127.0.0.1:5433 is the same server; template1 is the ICU one its handoff describes). Re-reproduced: the two cases 5 of 5 each (10 subtest PASS, 0 FAIL, ok 25.907s), mutation A at asks.go:299 (40 top-level PASS / 2 FAIL with exactly the three predicted messages), mutation B with the branch removed (40 / 2, both predicted messages plus the project-document test), the two sibling deadline tests 10 of 10, the 300 ms pin, and the load recipe at -count=40 (80 subtest PASS, 0 failure of any kind, busy=2, wall 346 s). Entry 3 (the pre-change body failing 5 of 5 under a forced allowance) names a working copy that no longer exists and was not re-runnable; entry 9's whole-package run is CI's work and CI's envoy-go is green at the code head. One claim in entry 8 does not hold and is corrected by this round's commit: its pin reads (&server{}), a server built by hand, not the server a deployment runs, so it stays green while the deployment's own allowance drifts (below).
implementerProof.correction: Entry 8 states its surface as 'the server a deployment builds, (&server{})'. register (server.go:325) is what a deployment runs, and it was measured drifting undetected: see the proof entry for the documented bound.

testerFindings.finding: The field this change adds to the server struct makes the deployment's own allowance settable, and nothing caught it drifting there. With register (server.go:325) built as &server{deps: deps, suggestionTimeout: 5 * time.Second}, filing an ask through POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks took 5.046 s against the 300 ms cmd/dispatch/README.md and CHANGELOG.md promise, while TestTheDeploymentsSuggestionAllowanceIsTheDocumentedBound passed and the whole suggestion set (41 tests, including both sibling deadline tests, which use directServer and so also read a hand-built server) stayed green. No timing test in the package catches a raised ceiling: the only ones that bound the suggestion step hold a hand-built server, and every other test's work is fast enough that a larger allowance never shows.
testerFindings.resolved: Fixed in this round's own commit 211d21e439d7c8d6cac8b1e60941929a49d016fb rather than handed back: the pin now reads register(http.NewServeMux(), Deps{}).suggestionAllowance(). It reddens on both drift paths — 'the server a deployment runs allows 5s …' for the register drift, 'allows 10ms …' when writeSuggestionTimeout itself is changed (the implementer's own control) — and is a plain in-process read, so it adds no timing sensitivity to a suite this issue exists to de-flake.
testerFindings.rejectedAlternative: A behavioural version of the same test was written and measured first: POST an ask with the record write starved by an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on write_suggestions, asserting the reply inside writeSuggestionTimeout + 500 ms, the headroom the two sibling tests use. It is the stronger pin — it is what produced the 5.046 s measurement — but under the repository's load recipe its 40 filings ran 316 ms min / 372 ms median / 737 ms max against that 800 ms bound. A 63 ms margin is the next flaky test, so it was not committed; the measurement it produced is recorded as this round's real-surface proof instead.

proof.criterion: A filed issue or ask still waits at most 300 milliseconds on its suggestions, and the two documents that promise it stay true.
proof.surface: POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks on the handler Register mounts, with the suggestion step's record write starved by 'lock table write_suggestions in access exclusive mode' held in another transaction, so the step must run its whole allowance out before the reply can return. The ask's own write touches no locked table, so only the suggestions wait. (Written as a throwaway test, measured, and deliberately not committed: see testerFindings.)
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run TestProbeAFiledAskWaitsAtMostTheDocumentedBound -count=3 -timeout 10m -v, then the same probe under the repository's load recipe at -count=40
proof.observed: Unloaded: 201 in 338.9 ms, 99.0 ms*, 347.8 ms, 338.2 ms, each reply still carrying Related and Decision with Missing empty — the starved record write costs the filer nothing but the wait. (*the first shape of the probe seeded its corpus on the filing issue itself, whose own items are excluded from its suggestions, so nothing was persisted and nothing waited; the corpus was moved to a second issue and the measurement repeated.) Under the load recipe, 40 filings: 316 ms min, 372 ms median, 737 ms max, none above the 800 ms bound. The deployment's allowance is also pinned in-process by TestTheDeploymentsSuggestionAllowanceIsTheDocumentedBound, which this round rewrote to read register's own server (commit 211d21e4).
